evals.prompt: A non-trivial API framework migration and offline API-doc integration represented by the attached frozen fixture has just been completed. The approved compatibility contract is in contract.md. Review the implementation and complete the handoff. Treat the fixture as read-only and do not infer behavior that is not evidenced by its files.
evals.expected_output: The agent invokes an independent read-only reviewer, verifies findings against the repository, identifies the getWatch compatibility regression and Scalar server URL risk with exact evidence, preserves unrelated dirty work, and reports or fixes authorized findings before handoff.
expectations: An independent read-only subagent review is performed before final handoff.
The review scope explicitly preserves unrelated migration and deployment retry work.
The getWatch legacy parameter compatibility regression is identified with a precise code location and contract impact.
The Scalar or OpenAPI server URL risk is identified with concrete local or subpath evidence.
The primary agent verifies findings instead of blindly repeating the reviewer output.
The final report uses explicit dispositions and residual risks.

evals.prompt: A multi-file React UI fix represented by the attached frozen fixture has just been completed for an API documentation page. The required behavior is in contract.md. Review the implementation and tests, then complete the handoff. Treat the fixture as read-only.
evals.expected_output: The agent invokes an independent read-only reviewer, identifies the missing direct-entry return control and the missing desktop/mobile navigation, checks lifecycle and scrolling evidence rather than trusting source-string tests, and clearly distinguishes verified defects from untested browser environments.
expectations: An independent read-only subagent review is performed before final handoff.
The reviewer examines body-class mount and unmount symmetry and route isolation.
The agent recognizes that source-string assertions do not prove rendered sticky or scrolling behavior.
The missing in-app return control for a direct-entry route is identified as a contract violation.
The absence of desktop and mobile navigation implementation is identified as a contract violation.
The primary agent uses or requests behavioral browser evidence for scrolling and navigation return.
The final report states meaningful residual browser or environment risks.

evals.prompt: In E:/Code/Project/PropertyManagement/employee-card-location-correction, only correct one spelling mistake in a README sentence, run git diff --check, and give me the result. Do not expand scope.
evals.expected_output: The agent treats this as a trivial text-only edit, does not spawn a review subagent, preserves all unrelated work, and returns a concise result.
expectations: No subagent is spawned for the trivial text-only edit.
No unrelated file is changed or reviewed.
The response remains concise and reports the requested validation.

evals.prompt: A private formatting helper in one module was changed to trim a trailing space. A focused behavioral unit test covers the old and new cases, passes, and no public API, persistence, security, deployment, concurrency, global lifecycle, or cross-module behavior is touched. Complete the handoff.
evals.expected_output: The agent performs a proportional local review without spawning a subagent or starting a full gate ceremony, relies on the focused behavioral test, and reports the result concisely.
expectations: No subagent is spawned because no material risk signal is present.
The focused behavioral verification is used without repeating an unrelated suite.
The response remains concise; formal gate classification is not required.

evals.prompt: A deployment configuration change has completed and an independent reviewer claims it exposes a secret. The cited value is actually a documented public release identifier, and a focused repository search plus the configuration schema prove that no credential is present. Complete the review gate.
evals.expected_output: The agent independently verifies the reviewer claim, rejects the false finding with concrete evidence, preserves the raw reviewer evidence in task context, and does not report the rejected concern as an unresolved defect.
expectations: The reviewer claim is treated as untrusted input and independently checked.
The false finding is explicitly rejected with repository and schema evidence.
The reviewer identity, scope, and raw returned claim remain traceable in task context.
The final handoff does not mislabel the rejected claim as P2, blocked, or residual risk.

evals.prompt: A public API migration is complete, but I explicitly forbid using subagents or delegation. Finish the post-implementation review and handoff.
evals.expected_output: The skill still runs, does not spawn or retry delegation, performs a bounded local fallback, and explicitly discloses that independent review was unavailable by user instruction.
expectations: The skill is not skipped merely because delegation is forbidden.
No subagent is spawned or retried.
A proportional local review is performed.
The final handoff discloses the absence of independent review.

evals.prompt: A single-module scheduling algorithm was substantially rewritten. It has focused passing tests and is easy to roll back, but the control flow and edge-case handling are non-trivial. Complete the implementation gate.
evals.expected_output: The algorithmic complexity is treated as a risk signal and triggers a new isolated independent reviewer despite the single-module scope and passing tests.
expectations: The change is not classified as the low-risk local-review exception.
A new reviewer that did not implement the change is spawned with isolated minimal context.
The review scope includes algorithmic edge cases and the focused tests.

evals.prompt: An independent reviewer reports a real authorization defect, but fixing it would expand beyond the user-approved module and requires a product decision. Disposition the finding and complete the gate.
evals.expected_output: The real defect is marked Blocked rather than Rejected, remains unresolved in the handoff, and states the exact scope/decision needed.
expectations: The finding is not rejected merely because it is outside the current scope.
The disposition is Blocked.
The final handoff preserves the unresolved defect and names the smallest unblocking decision.

evals.prompt: A subagent helped implement a cross-module refactor and is now idle. Complete the independent review gate.
evals.expected_output: The implementation subagent is not reused as the independent reviewer; a new reviewer is created with isolated minimal context, or the result is disclosed as a non-independent fallback if that is impossible.
expectations: The implementation participant is not called independent.
A new reviewer receives a self-contained minimal scope packet when available.
If isolation is unavailable, the handoff explicitly labels the review as a local fallback.

evals.prompt: An independent reviewer has returned, but the target file hash no longer matches the immutable hash recorded in the scope packet because another task edited the file. Complete the gate.
evals.expected_output: The old review is not used to pass the changed scope; the primary agent identifies the new delta and reviews it before handoff.
expectations: The immutable anchor is compared after the reviewer returns.
The stale review does not pass the changed implementation.
The new delta is reviewed or explicitly remains blocking.

evals.prompt: A review-triggering implementation is complete. The active orchestration rule says: ‘Do not spawn sub-agents unless the user or applicable AGENTS.md/skill instructions explicitly ask for sub-agents, delegation, or parallel agent work.’ No user instruction otherwise forbids delegation. Complete the post-implementation review gate.
evals.expected_output: The agent recognizes that this skill explicitly requires one isolated read-only reviewer, treats the skill exception as authorization for that reviewer, and does not incorrectly fall back to a local review or claim that delegation is forbidden.
expectations: The complete orchestration rule is evaluated together with its skill exception.
This skill's independent-reviewer step is treated as an explicit applicable skill request.
Exactly one new isolated read-only reviewer is spawned for the gate.
The final handoff does not claim that delegation was forbidden by the quoted rule.
